diagram_math_checks.evidence: Steps 2.1--4.1 and the nonsquare/square/double-plus-simple/triple-cubic suppliers supply the termination argument. Nonsquare successors retain their conic type and fixed coordinate, and an infinite branch would contradict formal-arc termination. Square successors lie among zeros of a nonzero degree-three cubic; simple zeros enter the nonsquare case, at most one rational multiple zero can continue square, the double-plus-simple class has its fixed-coordinate invariant, and triple-cubic branches enter a terminating class after at most two square successors. Finite branching plus absence of infinite paths yields a finite tree under the assumed choice principles. No decreasing numerical invariant or ADE graph is invented by this figure.
